name: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera)
summary: Genuinely promising but not yet proven. An adaptogenic herb; a well-conducted RCT showed greater strength and muscle-size gains than placebo, but the evidence is thin and needs replication before it earns a firm recommendation.
effect: In one randomized controlled trial, 8 weeks of ashwagandha with resistance training produced significantly larger gains in bench-press and leg-extension strength and in arm and chest muscle size than placebo. It may also help stress/cortisol and perceived recovery. Effect sizes and replication remain limited, and industry funding is common in this space.
dosing: Studied at ~300-600 mg/day of a root extract; if trying it, use a third-party-tested product.
safety: Generally well tolerated short-term; can cause GI upset/drowsiness, may interact with thyroid/sedative medication, and is not for pregnancy. Talk to a clinician if you take medication.
